clue.text: An opening in the ground!

parts.note: reads like a hole dug in the earth, but means the start of a match at a football ground

explanation.surface: Someone points out a hole in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ground' is a sports ground, and the 'opening' is the first moment of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of a football match, when the ball is first struck, is its opening.

clue.text: What prince becomes with a drinking vessel and a flower

parts.note: a prince succeeds to the throne as monarch
a cup is a vessel to drink from

explanation.surface: A prince is crowned with a goblet and a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh marigold, the yellow buttercup-like bloom of wet ground.

clue.text: Seal off a road

definitions.meaning: a cul-de-sac or residential street, often named this in Britain

explanation.surface: Police barring access to a street.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word is common in street names for a dead-end road.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut is to seal; a dead-end street in Britain is often named this.

clue.text: Drunk given a shot out of a can

definitions.text: given a shot out of a can
definitions.meaning: squirted with lubricant from an oilcan

explanation.surface: Someone inebriated after a drink from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot out of a can' sounds like a canned drink; it is a squirt from an oilcan.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for tipsy, and also lubricated by a squirt from an oilcan.

clue.text: Dug fire-break, it's reckoned

indicators.note: break means the letters are smashed apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone excavated a firebreak, or so it is thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire-break' looks like one word; 'break' is the anagram signal on DUG FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have worked something out or estimated it is to have calculated it.

clue.text: His shop always offers cut prices

definitions.text: His shop always offers cut prices

parts.words: His shop always offers cut prices
parts.note: sounds like a discount shop, but the prices are for cuts of meat

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who never stops offering discounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut prices' suggests bargains; here it means the prices of cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat trader sells joints and chops, all priced by the cut.

clue.text: Having a chance to make money?

definitions.text: Having a chance to make money?

parts.words: Having a chance to make money?
parts.note: sounds like an opportunity; it is literally having a flutter on chance

explanation.surface: Being given an opportunity to earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a chance' reads as being offered an opportunity, but means taking a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagering stakes on an uncertain outcome is gambling to win money.

clue.text: Film-set, happen

parts.note: to film is to take a shot
to set something down is to place it

explanation.surface: A film set where something is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film-set' looks like a studio; split into two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur or come about is the meaning of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Result of a very good-or very bad!-shot

definitions.text: Result of a very good-or very bad!-shot

parts.words: Result of a very good-or very bad!-shot
parts.note: a golf ace is a superb stroke; the joke is it also suggests a terrible shot into a pit

explanation.surface: Musing on outcomes of an excellent or terrible attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf it is a single stroke from tee to cup; a very bad shot might also end in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's ace, the ball sinking from the tee in a single stroke.

clue.text: Is left behind to die; sure is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to leave someone to perish, which is plainly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DIE and SURE; 'Is left behind' is what the noun names: whatever remains.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest is removed is the remainder or leftover.

clue.text: A bright idea of the advertisers?

definitions.text: A bright idea of the advertisers?

parts.words: A bright idea of the advertisers?
parts.note: a 'bright idea' is normally a clever thought; here it is a literally glowing sign

explanation.surface: Advertising folk come up with a clever scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bright idea' is taken literally: a glowing tube sign used in advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled tube signs are a classic advertisers' device for shopfronts.

clue.text: It's most likely put back in these clothes

indicators.note: put back tells us the run of letters is read in the reverse direction
in signals the letters sit inside the words most likely

explanation.surface: A guess about where something was most probably returned among garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses STLIK, the run hidden 'in' moST LIKely.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleated tartan skirts worn as traditional Scottish dress are garments.

clue.text: Gorge this dairy product?

definitions.meaning: a gorge in the Mendip Hills of Somerset, England, a famous limestone ravine
a hard cheese named after that Somerset village

explanation.surface: An invitation to stuff yourself on a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb, eat greedily; it is the noun, the Somerset ravine that gives the cheese its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset ravine and the hard cheese both carry the same village name.

clue.text: It's suggested I limped off

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they hobbled away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hinted at without being stated outright has been suggested.

clue.text: RUC back-up for this member of the Force?

definitions.text: RUC back-up for this member of the Force?

parts.words: RUC back-up for this member of the Force?
parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary; its back-up member is a canine one

explanation.surface: Asking about reinforcements for a Northern Ireland police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001; a 'member of the Force' sounds human but here has four legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained animal working with officers is a canine member of the police.

clue.text: Peer marries tart in haste

parts.note: to peer is to look
tart means sour or sharp-tasting

explanation.surface: A nobleman hurriedly weds a loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord and 'tart' a woman; they are a verb and an adjective. 'marries' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to hurry up, said as an idiom: be quick about it.

clue.text: Take a bath before turning up to confess?

definitions.text: Take a bath before turning up to confess?

parts.words: Take a bath before turning up to confess?
parts.note: read literally, arrive washed; idiomatically, own up

explanation.surface: Advice to wash before arriving to make a confession.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, washing before you arrive means you arrive spotless; the idiom means to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for admitting the truth or owning up to wrongdoing.

clue.text: A 50-1 horse in a walk-over!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
one written out as a word

explanation.surface: Betting odds of fifty to one on a horse in an uncontested race.
explanation.walkthrough: '50-1' looks like betting odds; it is split into L and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a walk-over a single horse runs unopposed, with no other runner beside it.

clue.text: Create a disturbance in the atmosphere!

definitions.text: Create a disturbance in the atmosphere!

parts.words: Create a disturbance in the atmosphere!
parts.note: reads as making a scene in a tense room, and as weather upheaval in the sky

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scene and spoils the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atmosphere' can be a room's mood or the air above us; the answer covers both a tantrum and bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage loudly is to cause a scene; a gale with rain is upheaval in the sky.

clue.text: Boxer on the ropes?

parts.note: a boxer trapped against the ring ropes; here one training with a jump rope

explanation.surface: A fighter pinned against the ring's ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the ropes' means in trouble in the ring; here it is a boxer training with a jump rope. The answer is also a captain, who works with ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jumping a rope, a staple of boxing training, is doing just that.

clue.text: Isn't like your normal novel

definitions.meaning: novel means new or unusual, unlike your normal

explanation.surface: An unusual work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unlike something, or new and unusual, both describe a thing that varies from others.

clue.text: Talk about a hellish oath!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the city of hell in Dante
a cuss is a swear word

explanation.surface: Discussing a fiendish curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate or talk over a subject is to examine it in conversation.

clue.text: Jet for Jack Dempsey, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an American heavyweight boxing champion of the 1920s

explanation.surface: An aircraft named after a famous boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dempsey was world heavyweight boxing champion from 1919 to 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: A warplane built for combat, and a boxer such as Dempsey, share this name.

clue.text: Couple who made old Bob hide their work

definitions.text: Couple who made old Bob hide their work

parts.words: Couple who made old Bob hide their work
parts.note: two old sixpences made a shilling, called a bob; leather workers treat animal hides

explanation.surface: A pair forced an elderly man named Bob to conceal what they did.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British money a 'tanner' was sixpence and a 'bob' a shilling, so a couple of them made a bob; 'hide' is also animal skin cured into leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Two old sixpenny coins made a shilling, and leather curers work on animal skins.

clue.text: A great part of life it's left scientists confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters that remain are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A claim that something has left researchers bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' means take away: remove the letters of IT'S from SCIENTISTS and 'confused' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs make up a huge share of animal species on Earth, so they are much of living things.

clue.text: Big pipe lighters supplied by it

definitions.text: Big pipe lighters supplied by it

parts.words: Big pipe lighters supplied by it
parts.note: sounds like matches for a smoker's pipe; the pipe is a large conduit feeding cookers

explanation.surface: Large tobacco pipes need their own matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big pipe' suggests a smoker; it is a large underground conduit carrying fuel to gas lighters and burners.
explanation.definitionFit: The large underground conduit carrying fuel to homes supplies gas lighters and burners.

clue.text: One with a job stacking brushes!

definitions.text: One with a job stacking brushes!

parts.words: One with a job stacking brushes!
parts.note: sounds like a shop worker; the job is cleaning chimney stacks with brushes

explanation.surface: A shelf-filler whose task is piling up brooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacking' looks like piling up; the 'stack' is a chimney stack, cleaned with brushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney cleaner, who pushes brushes up the flue, does exactly this job.

clue.text: What English girl might love in Siam girl

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the girl's name

parts.note: Anna Leonowens, the English governess in Siam of The King and I
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: A Siamese girl might be the object of an English girl's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna is the governess at the court of Siam in 'Anna and the King of Siam'; love is a score of nil, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name of English use, so it labels a girl.

clue.text: A trophy for helping

definitions.meaning: a cup or dish given as a prize, as in racing
a serving of food on a dish

explanation.surface: A trophy awarded for being helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like assisting; it is a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish-shaped prize and a portion served at a meal share the same word.

clue.text: Like standard definition of lunacy

parts.note: a standard is a flagpole, so going up one is a slang phrase for madness

explanation.surface: Quoting the usual dictionary meaning of insanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like usual but is a flagpole; the British slang phrase for 'crazy' describes climbing one.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for crazy or mistaken, literally climbing a flagpole.

clue.text: Is sorry for past & present difficulties

indicators.note: difficulties suggests trouble or disorder, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the troubles of then and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past & present' reads as a pair; 'past' goes with the definition and 'present' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse for earlier wrongs is exactly what someone contrite does.

clue.text: Films in the Screen Two series?

definitions.text: Films in the Screen Two series?

parts.words: Films in the Screen Two series?
parts.note: Screen Two was a BBC drama strand; read as screened twice, films shown a second time

explanation.surface: Asking what films appear in a BBC television drama strand.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen Two was a BBC2 film series; 'Screen Two' also reads as screen a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts shown a second time are rebroadcasts, screened once more.
